summary: Since a 2023 presidential decree Angola waives visas for tourists from the 98 countries and territories on the SME eVisa portal's exemption list (as of 8 October 2026) — including the EU, UK, US, China and Japan — for stays of up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year. Mozambique, Namibia, São Tomé and Príncipe, South Africa and Zambia are also exempt for short stays under bilateral agreements. Everyone else applies for a tourist eVisa through the SME portal, and WHO lists a yellow fever certificate as required from all travellers aged 9 months or over.

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says non-residents must declare cash or travellers cheques worth USD 5,000 or more (USD 10,000 for residents) and keep the certified declaration, that you cannot take out more than USD 5,000 (USD 10,000 for residents), and that up to 50,000 kwanzas in cash may be taken out in addition. The Government of Canada says kwanzas cannot be taken out of the country.

conflict.name: Government of Canada — Angola travel advice: money
conflict.states: Kwanzas cannot be taken out of the country; no more than US$15,000 can be taken into or out of Angola unless an official declaration is made upon entry.

notes: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to take turtle shells or ivory out of Angola, and that customs may keep handicrafts considered to be of cultural value.

Canada advises against photographing airports, major roads, bridges, communications installations, military personnel and government buildings, and the UK warns not to use cameras, binoculars or GPS equipment near government buildings.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are accepted at only a few of Luanda's largest hotels and restaurants, VISA most often, that ATMs dispense only kwanzas and often malfunction or run out of cash, and that dollars can be changed for kwanzas at the few exchange bureaus in Luanda or at local banks.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says there is a high level of crime in Luanda, some of it violent, and advises not walking around Luanda, especially alone or after dark. It says roads outside Luanda and the provincial capitals are often in poor condition, and advises against all but essential travel to Cabinda Province, except Cabinda city, because separatist groups have carried out targeted attacks on foreigners.

tips.text: Visa-free entry under Presidential Decree 189/23 is for tourism: up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year.
WHO lists Angola as requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination from all travellers aged 9 months or over, and the SME eVisa application asks for an international vaccination certificate.

The UK Foreign Office says you can take out up to 50,000 kwanzas in cash; the Government of Canada says kwanzas cannot be taken out of the country, and that involvement in black-market currency conversion could lead to arrest.
Canada's travel advice notes that many doctors and medical staff, including in Luanda, speak Portuguese rather than English or French.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Angola?
faq.answer: Citizens of the 98 countries and territories on the SME eVisa portal's exemption list (as of 8 October 2026) — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, China and Japan — have been visa-exempt for tourism since Angola's 2023 decree, for stays of up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year. Mozambique, Namibia, São Tomé and Príncipe, South Africa and Zambia are also exempt for short stays under bilateral agreements. Everyone else applies for a tourist eVisa via the official SME portal or for a visa at an Angolan embassy or consulate.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Angola visa-free?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year. The SME says a tourist visa allows a stay of up to 30 days and can be extended once for an equal period.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Angola?
faq.answer: Yes — WHO lists Angola as requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination from all travellers aged 9 months or over, regardless of where they fly from.

faq.question: How does the Angola eVisa work?
faq.answer: You apply online through the SME portal. The portal says applications are processed in 72 hours and that, if approved, the entry visa is sent by email and must be presented on arrival in Angola. The SME eVisa FAQ gives the fee as Kz 36,600, paid in cash at the border.

faq.question: What documents do I need at the Angolan border?
faq.answer: The eVisa portal's form instructions ask for a passport with at least 4 empty pages; the UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after you arrive and have 2 blank pages, and WHO lists a yellow fever certificate as required from all travellers aged 9 months or over. eVisa applicants must also upload a round-trip flight booking, an accommodation booking and proof of financial means.
